[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll get started in a minute. I'm Maya Chen, I'm the AE on the account, and with me is Rafael from our SRE/SE team.
[00:18] Rafael: hi all hello, thanks for making time. quick agenda: show Hosted API embeddings, rerank endpoints, then jump into Console to show cost/latency traces and Optimize recommendations.
[00:32] Jordan: sounds good, we wanna see how this fits into our current search stack, right now we run Elastic + a vector store and we're seeing ranking issues esp for multi-turn queries.
[00:45] Priya: yeah and latency matters, p50 needs to be under 120ms for search suggestions but for full rerank we can tolerate a bit more.
[00:57] Marcus: security posture is a hard requirement; SOC2, SSO/SAML, and KMS for key management — we also need audit logs for queries.
[01:12] Maya: great, we will hit those. Rafael, maybe start the demo?
[01:16] Rafael: sure, sharing screen. so here is the hosted embeddings endpoint: /v1/embeddings, we send a short doc or query, we get back a 1536-d vector (depends on model), vector normalized, and timestamp. example request... (shows curl) — curl -X POST /v1/embeddings -d '{"input":"best restaurants in seattle"}'
[01:45] Jordan: quick question — do you do on-the-fly normalization or do you recommend client-side?
[01:51] Rafael: we normalize server-side by default, but clients can opt-out. small transcription glitch: "nor-muh-lize" sometimes shows up in the automated notes, but we do it server-side so it simplifies pipelines.
[02:05] Rafael: next, the rerank endpoint — this is the part a lot of customers use to improve ML-based ordering. we accept a query + list of candidate documents (ids + optional embeddings) and we return a score per candidate and a reranked list. payload is JSON, example: {"query":"...","candidates":[{"id":"123","embedding": [...]}, ...]}
[02:30] Priya: do you compute embeddings inside rerank if we don't send them?
[02:35] Rafael: yes, you can send raw texts for candidates, or precomputed embeddings. sending embeddings saves compute if you already store them in your vector DB. for latency-sensitive flows we recommend pre-computing and storing embeddings and passing them to rerank.
[02:51] Jordan: what's the typical p95 for rerank when sending precomputed embeddings?
[02:55] Rafael: for hosted we typically see p95 around 160-220ms for lists of 50 candidates with our default model; p50 can be ~60-90ms depending on sequence length. this varies with model choice and batch sizing. it's also worth noting our console shows per-route traces so you can see token time breakdowns.
[03:16] Marcus: what about cost vs latency — if we need p50 <120ms for suggestions, is it cheaper to do fewer candidates + rerank vs heavier vector-store recall?
[03:26] Rafael: yes tradeoffs. Optimize will recommend batching/caching profiles. e.g., prefix caching for frequent queries can drop per-request token counts a lot. Also we recommend a hybrid approach: use recall to limit to top-N candidates (e.g., 100) then rerank. for suggestions you could use smaller candidate sets.
[03:42] Priya: do you support automatic candidate pruning?
[03:45] Rafael: not automatic in the API, but our SDKs + console examples show recall heuristics and shard-level scoring. we'll include a sample script.
[03:53] Jordan: can you show the Console now?
[03:56] Rafael: switching to Console. here is the model route for embeddings-rerank-demo, you can see request rates, latency histograms, token counts and cost per token. Also the traces tab — here's a single rerank request trace showing embedding compute + scoring + serialization.
[04:20] Maya: you mentioned Optimize — can you expand on what recommendations we'll see?
[04:25] Rafael: sure. Optimize looks at your traffic profile and suggests batch sizes, cache TTLs, and quantization profiles tailored to your model choices. for instance, if you have low-latency single-candidate flows, it may suggest a smaller batch and a lower-precision quantization to save cost. for heavy rerank jobs, it might suggest reserved capacity or dedicated pools to get predictable p95.
[04:46] Priya: reserved capacity - is that Redwood Dedicated? and do you have burst options?
[04:50] Rafael: Dedicated is for reserved GPU pools and yes, you can configure burst and autoscaling policies. for a pilot the hosted API is often faster to get started.
[04:58] Jordan: data isolation? our logs and raw queries cannot leave our VPC, ideally.
[05:03] Maya: we have Redwood Private for VPC/on-prem and a Private control plane option. hosted API is multi-tenant but we have strict data retention and encryption; however for strict isolation you'd look at Private. we can scope that in the POC if needed.
[05:18] Marcus: SOC2 and KMS — do you offer customer-managed keys?
[05:22] Maya: yes KMS integrations available for Private and Dedicated; for hosted we support BYOK with partner KMS in some regions — we'll share the security pack.
[05:31] Priya: how does rerank work with our existing vector store? we use Pinecone for recall currently.
[05:36] Rafael: common pattern: keep Pinecone for ANN recall, return top-200 ids, fetch documents, compute or fetch embeddings, call /rerank with those embeddings, get ordered list. This avoids moving large vectors through your app repeatedly. We'll share sample code for Pinecone + Redwood rerank.
[05:54] Jordan: can you run a quick live example with a small candidate list?
[05:58] Rafael: yep, I'll demo a curl with 5 candidates. (typing) sending request... response comes back — shows scores and reranked list. the transcript auto caption shows "scores come back slick" which is obviously a mis-hear — it was "scores come back quick".
[06:25] Jordan: nice — score distribution looks reasonable. do you return explainability info? like token-level attention or contribution?
[06:32] Rafael: we expose a lightweight explain endpoint — you can request per-candidate feature responses (e.g., similarity score, model logit) but we avoid returning full attention matrices for size. for regulatory use-cases we have options to redact or limit explain outputs.
[06:47] Priya: on billing, is it per token for embeddings + per-call for rerank?
[06:53] Maya: embeddings billed per embedding call (per input tokens + model), rerank billed per request + token consumption; we can provide a unit economics spreadsheet. Optimize will also estimate cost savings from batching and caching.
[07:07] Marcus: do you have SLAs for hosted route latency?
[07:11] Maya: hosted has best-effort with region-level SLOs; Dedicated includes SLA-backed uptime and latency targets. we'll put numbers in the pricing pack.
[07:20] Jordan: sample logs — Priya will share them after this call right?
[07:24] Priya: yes I can grab anonymized logs, it's about a week of queries  —  we'll scrub PII.
[07:31] Rafael: perfect, once we have logs we can run a small benchmark using your real query distribution and show expected p50/p95 and cost estimates.
[07:40] Jordan: any integration with our analytics stack for tracing? we use Datadog.
[07:45] Rafael: yes we have tracing hooks and can forward traces to Datadog; Console also has exportable traces and per-route metrics.
[07:54] Marcus: latency under load — we see spikes during peak product launch periods, can you do autoscaling fast enough?
[07:59] Rafael: realtime autoscaling helps, but for predictable peak we recommend Dedicated with autoscale policies. for hosted we have regional burst capacity and fallback to a cheaper model if capacity tightens.
[08:13] Priya: what's the expected developer effort to swap our rerank call to Redwood?
[08:18] Rafael: minimal — you need to add a client call to our rerank endpoint and optionally store embeddings; SDKs in Python/Node will be a few lines. we'll share code samples.
[08:29] Jordan: can we see the sample SDK snippet?
[08:31] Rafael: sharing code now in chat — python sample: from redwood import Client; client.rerank(query, candidates=[...]) — returns scores. (automated caption shows 'from red wood' once again)
[08:45] Maya: we also wanted to show Optimize's recommended quantization profiles — Rafael can show an example where switching to q4_0 saved 30% cost with minimal quality drop on synthetic eval.
[08:56] Rafael: yep, here's Optimize recommendations for a simulated search workload: suggested quantize q4_0 for the model, cache TTL 60s for top queries, batch size 8 for rerank path. Estimated cost drop ~28% while p95 increased by ~15ms.
[09:16] Priya: curious, does Optimize tie recommendations to our regression alerts? we want to avoid quality regressions when changing quantization.
[09:22] Rafael: yes, Optimize integrates with our evals — you can run A/B tests and have quality gating; the Console flags regressions against your golden prompt set.
[09:33] Jordan: want to circle back to data residency — we need EU-only for some customers.
[09:38] Maya: we have region pinning in hosted and full private for EU-only deployments. for highly regulated data we recommend Private.
[09:45] Marcus: alright, any downsides to hosted for our pilot?
[09:48] Rafael: tradeoff is isolation vs time-to-market — hosted gets you running quickly, but if you need strict VPC/KMS it adds onboarding time to set up Private or Dedicated.
[10:00] Jordan: could you show a sample rerank payload size and cost estimate for 200 candidates?
[10:04] Rafael: sure — quickly: 200 candidates with 1536-d vectors is about X MB payload going into rerank; cost scales with token consumption and model. We typically recommend narrowing candidate sets to 50-100 with ANN recall to keep latency low. we'll compute exact numbers in the benchmark spreadsheet.
[10:29] Priya: what's the max candidate list size supported in a single rerank call?
[10:33] Rafael: current practical limit is ~1000 candidates but performance degrades; we advise under 500 for production real-time paths.
[10:41] Jordan: okay got it. can we talk about POC success criteria? what would you recommend?
[10:48] Maya: success criteria we usually suggest: measurable improvement in NDCG/MRR on your test set, acceptable p95 latency (we'll calibrate), and cost within target. Rafael: and operational: integration completed, traces enabled, alerts set.
[11:02] Marcus: timeline — we want a POC within 2 weeks. is that feasible?
[11:07] Rafael: yes, with logs and sample data we can run an initial bench within 3-5 business days and then a pilot.
[11:14] Jordan: any legal or procurement blockers we should expect?
[11:17] Maya: standard NDAs and an MSA for pilot; for Private there are more security addendums. We'll send procurement docs.
[11:25] Priya: how do you handle query-level PII that might exist in logs?
[11:30] Maya: we recommend anonymization on your side, but we also offer automated redaction options; for Private you can keep full control.
[11:36] Rafael: demo note: response times in terminal are slightly faster than Console due to local caching in the demo environment, real world depends on region.

[11:49] Rafael: console supports per-route breakdowns, token-level cost, and a tracing UI to drill into model and network time.
